title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: when a missing excess withdrawal fee is charged on reconciliation, and on which withdrawal
content:
## Scope

This rule applies to a Savings & Money Market Accounts account from which overdraft protection transfers have been made, when the excess withdrawal fees of a statement cycle are reconciled. It combines the withdrawals that need a fee, the withdrawals fees already cover and the fees that may still be charged, and decides whether a fee is charged, how much, and on which withdrawal.

## Policy clause

1. The fees outstanding are the counted withdrawals beyond the allowance that no fee covers, but no more than the fees that may still be charged in the cycle, and never below none.
2. When at least one fee is outstanding, an excess withdrawal fee is charged at the tier's excess withdrawal fee on the earliest counted withdrawal beyond the allowance, in posting order, that carries no fee, and it is posted as one excess withdrawal fee for that cycle attached to that withdrawal.
3. Each further outstanding fee is a separate entry of the same amount on the next such withdrawal.
4. When no fee is outstanding, nothing is charged under this rule.

## Order of the calculation

1. Take the counted withdrawals beyond the allowance that need a fee.
2. Take away the withdrawals that fees already cover.
3. If the difference is larger than the fees that may still be charged, take that smaller number.
4. If the figure is below zero, take none.

## Comparison table

| Withdrawals needing a fee | Withdrawals already covered | Fees that may still be charged | Fees outstanding |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 2 | 4 | 1 |
| 4 | 2 | 4 | 2, on two different withdrawals |
| 3 | 1 | 1 | 1; the fees that may still be charged limit it |
| 2 | 2 | 3 | none |
| 1 | 2 | 3 | none; the difference is below zero |

## Worked case (hypothetical cycle; the allowance of 3 is illustrative, not a tier value)

The counted withdrawals of the cycle, in posting order, are W1 to W6; W1 to W3 are within the allowance, so W4, W5 and W6 each need a fee. W4 and W5 each carry a fee that covers them. W6 carries none. One fee is outstanding, provided at least one fee may still be charged in the cycle. It is posted at the tier's excess withdrawal fee, for that cycle, attached to W6, the earliest counted withdrawal beyond the allowance that carries no fee.

## Points of judgement

**Wrong reading:** "Put the fee on the most recent withdrawal." **Correct basis:** it goes on the earliest counted withdrawal beyond the allowance, in posting order, that carries no fee.

**Wrong reading:** "Post one combined entry for all outstanding fees." **Correct basis:** each outstanding fee is a separate entry of the same amount on its own withdrawal.

**Can a withdrawal within the allowance receive the fee?** No; only a counted withdrawal beyond the allowance.
